podcast.title: Treble Charger Formation (1992) – Original Name NC17
podcast.body: The band formed in Sault Ste. Marie in 1992, initially under the name NC17, inspired by the American movie rating. "They originally came from Susanne Marie in 1992 under the name NC17, like the American movie rating."

podcast.title: Treble Charger Breakup (February 2006)
podcast.body: The band concluded its 14-year run in February 2006, deciding it was simply "time" to end. "The band had a 14 year run coming to an end in February 2006. It was just time."

podcast.title: Bill Priddle's Work with Broken Social Scene
podcast.body: After Treble Charger disbanded, guitarist Bill Priddle dedicated more time to working with Broken Social Scene. "Guitarist Bill Prittle wanted to spend more time working with Broken Social Scene which he has."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: CD-ROM Interactive Content
podcast.body: The CD-ROM portion of the *Self Title* re-release featured a digital scene showcasing some of Treble Charger's "Can Rock" friends, a feature considered "groundbreaking" and "really cool" for its era. "If you stuck this thing into your computer, you were rewarded with a digital scene that featured some of treble chargers, Ken Rock, friends, really nice gesture, really cool for 1995 or 2006 or whenever it came out."

podcast.title: Early Mentors of Sum 41
podcast.body: Greg Norrie, a member of Trevor Charger, became a friend and early mentor to Sum 41, along with Marcos Stanzo of Len. Norrie provided crucial support by helping with demos, offering advice, and bringing the nascent band on tour. "Greg Norrie from Trevor Charger?"

podcast.body: Greg Nori was a member of Treble Charger for decades before moving into band management and production. "Greg has been a member of treble charger for decades..."

podcast.title: Greig Nori's Management and Production Career
podcast.body: Singer Greig Nori became actively involved in managing and producing Sum 41, a band he discovered. He also managed other bands, worked with beer companies, and secured various television gigs. "Singer Greg Norrie has had his hands full with managing and producing a band he discovered. You might have heard of them, they're called Sum41."

podcast.body: Another former drummer, Morris Paller, obtained a degree in contemporary percussion performance and is now highly sought after by composers globally. "And another former drummer, Morris Paltar, now has a degree in contemporary percussion performance and is sought out by composers around the world."

podcast.title: Name Change to Treble Charger
podcast.body: The band changed its name to Treble Charger after an American band already using "NC17" threatened legal action. "So rather than fight that, they changed their name to treble charger."

podcast.body: The re-release of *Self Title* was very successful, earning the band a Juno nomination for Best Alternative Album. "The re-release of self equal title worked out very well, resulting in a June nomination for Best Alternative Album."

xref.title: Career Shift
xref.body: Greg Nori was a member of the band Treble Charger for decades, but has since diversified into band management and production. "Greg has been a member of treble charger for decades but now he's branched off into band management and production."

xref.title: Vocal Style Development
xref.body: Ben, the vocalist, initially spent the first five years of the band trying to emulate other singers like Eddie Vedder, Scott Weiland, and Zack de la Rocha. He eventually realized he couldn't sound like them and developed his own distinctive style. This unique vocal approach, combined with Ian's guitar playing, helped the band stand out from other Canadian bands of the era like Moist, Treble Charger, and The Tea Party. "I, the first five years of being in a band, you know, I was trying to sound like other people, you know, I was trying to sound like Eddie Vetter. I was trying to sound like Scott Watt. I'm trying to sound like Zack Delroch. You know, like, I'm trying to do that. And then I realized I can't do that, you know, so I just kind of ended up being me."
